2610.13821.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
2610.13821.paper_summary: A useful language model should know when to answer and when to say "I don't know." Can we improve that decision by training the model itself or by training a separate component to check its answers? We study both approaches on Qwen3-14B for factual questions, using a score that rewards correct answers, penalizes mistakes, and allows abstention. Across three training seeds and two held-out confidence thresholds, a learned answer selector improves threshold-averaged utility over the original model's calibrated confidence filter. On TriviaQA, mean coverage increases from 20.2% to 30.9%, while the pooled error rate among scored answers decreases from 23.0% to 14.5% under exact-match grading. The tested reinforcement-learning changes do not establish consistent gains. On NQ-Open, the selector improves threshold-averaged utility over the filter but still performs worse than always abstaining. A partial human-reviewed audit preserves the TriviaQA finding. Our results support learning to select answers in this setting while showing that reliable abstention across datasets remains unresolved.
2610.13821.paper_summary_zh: 一個有用的語言模型應該知道何時回答以及何時說「我不知道」。我們能否通過訓練模型本身或訓練一個獨立的組件來檢查其答案來改善這一決策？我們在 Qwen3-14B 上研究這兩種方法，針對事實性問題，使用一個獎勵正確答案、懲罰錯誤並允許不作答的分數。在三個訓練種子和兩個保留的信心閾值下，學習的答案選擇器提高了閾值平均效用，超過了原始模型的校準信心過濾器。在 TriviaQA 上，平均覆蓋率從 20.2% 增加到 30.9%，而在精確匹配評分下，得分答案的總體錯誤率從 23.0% 降低到 14.5%。測試的強化學習變化並未建立一致的增益。在 NQ-Open 上，選擇器提高了閾值平均效用，但仍然表現不如始終不作答。部分人類審核的審計保留了 TriviaQA 的發現。我們的結果支持在這種情境下學習選擇答案，同時顯示在數據集之間可靠的不作答仍然未得到解決。
